To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cuticular proteins are transported to the cuticle surface in vesicles and that the cuticle surface is stabilized with polyphenols.
the distribution of phenoloxidase and polyphenol during cuticle formation in Colpodes etihus has been studied.
phenoloxidase is synthesized in the epidermal cell, transported in the Golgi complex to the cell surface and incorporated into the cuticle during its formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution of phenol oxidase and polyphenol in the cuticular environment.
the distribution and function of phenoloxidates and polyphenols in the cuticular formation of Colpodes ethicus.
the distribution of phenol oxidases and polyphenol oxidase in the epidermal cells of the 4th and 5th instars of Colpodes ethiops.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cuticular phenoloxidase is a component of the cuticle which is stabilized in the cuticle as a protein.
phenoloxidase is a component of the cuticle and the epicuticle and that it is deposited in the epicuticle as it is formed.
the epicuticle is a composite material which includes a cuticulin layer, an outer layer of protein and lipid, an inner layer of protein and quinones and an innermost layer of fibrous cuticle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the epicuticle is formed from a liquid crystal and that the epocuticle is formed by the deposition of cuticular proteins on the surface of the cuticulins.

cuticle formation in C. ethius is a process of stabilization of a liquid crystalline phase by the incorporation of protein, lipids and polyphenols, with the phenoloxidases acting as catalysts in the stabilization process.

cuticular phenoloxidase is synthesized in the epidermal cells, transported to the apices of the epidermal cell processes and incorporated into the epicuticle and epocuticle, and later into the fibrous cuticle of the exoskeleton.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cuticular environment is very dynamic and is constantly undergoing changes in its chemical composition.

phenoloxidase is present in the epicuticular layer and the epicuticular fibers, and the phenoloxidases may have been transported to the apicale face by vesicles, but there are still some gaps in our understanding.
cuticle formation in Colpodes is very different from that of other arthropods.
